## Overview

This unversioned [[adyen]] documentation page describes the accessibility purpose of Web Drop-in and Components, Adyen's Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT), the WCAG 2.1 standard and its POUR principles, and a version-qualified accessibility statement. It routes accessibility evidence for the [[adyen-online-payments]] web surfaces; it does not establish accessibility or legal compliance for a merchant's complete checkout.

## Key takeaways

- The page defines digital accessibility as designing and developing digital products so people with disabilities can use and interact with them effectively. Its product scope is Web Drop-in and Components, not every Adyen product or a merchant's surrounding checkout.
- A VPAT is described as a standardized document through which a vendor reports a product or service's accessibility, particularly for public-sector or accessibility-focused procurement. The page says Adyen partnered with Level Access to obtain a VPAT for Web Drop-in and Components and that those surfaces were tested against all criteria in WCAG 2.1.
- The page describes WCAG 2.1 as a W3C Web Accessibility Initiative framework covering visual, auditory, cognitive, and motor disabilities. It summarizes the four POUR principles: perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust.
- Adyen states that Web Drop-in and Components meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA and reports a "flawless Level AA rating" for version `5.49.0` or later. The page recommends upgrading to `5.49.0` or later to use the documented accessibility improvements.
- The version claim is a statement in this captured Adyen page, last modified in 2023 and fetched on 2026-09-15. The linked Checkout Web VPAT PDF was not included in or read as part of this raw snapshot. Treat the source as a locator to the reported assessment, not as an independent audit, a guarantee about every later release or configuration, or proof that a merchant's end-to-end experience satisfies current accessibility laws or standards.

quotes.text: Find out how Drop-in and Components optimize accessibility for your shoppers.

A Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) is a standardized document created to assess the accessibility of a product or service. It allows product vendors to provide potential customers with detailed information about the level of accessibility in their offerings, particularly for those in the public sector or organizations with accessibility procurement requirements.
quotes.location: line 33 under ## Voluntary Product Accessibility Template

quotes.text: Adyen has partnered up with [Level Access](https://www.levelaccess.com/) to obtain a VPAT for [Web Drop-in](/online-payments/build-your-integration/sessions-flow/?platform=Web\&integration=Drop-in) and [Components](/online-payments/build-your-integration/sessions-flow?platform=Web\&integration=Components). In this document, the performance of Web Drop-in and Components is tested against all the criteria included in Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1.
quotes.location: line 35 under ## Voluntary Product Accessibility Template

quotes.text: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 is a set of guidelines developed by the Web Accessibility Initiative (WAI) of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C). It provides a framework for making web content more accessible to people with disabilities. WCAG covers a wide range of disabilities, including visual, auditory, cognitive, and motor impairments.
quotes.location: line 39 under ## Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1

quotes.text:
At Adyen, we take digital accessibility seriously. Our commitment to inclusivity means that we diligently follow WCAG 2.1 guidelines, ensuring that Drop-in and Components meet the Level AA conformance level. The Level AA criteria from WCAG 2.1 are appointed as a standard of best practice for compliance.

Through rigorous testing and continuous improvement, we have obtained a flawless Level AA rating (supported by the VPAT available for download below), ensuring that Web Drop-in and Components [v5.49.0](/online-payments/release-notes/#releaseNote=2023-07-17-web-componentsdrop-in-5.49.0) or later are accessible to the widest possible audience.
